2026-09-01T03:28:06.4943582Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4943955Z 
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4944265Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4944746Z 
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4945132Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4945612Z 
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4947125Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4959468Z >
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4961759Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4964127Z >
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4964911Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4965670Z 
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4965846Z ### How to Use
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4966085Z 
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4966766Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4967474Z 
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4967651Z ```bash
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4968494Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4969223Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4969826Z ```
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4970032Z 
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4970298Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4970833Z ```bash
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4971377Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4972158Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4972991Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4973720Z ```
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4973930Z 
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4974541Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4975398Z ```bash
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4975960Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4976634Z ```
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4976881Z 
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4977358Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4978543Z ```bash
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4979092Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4979955Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4980646Z ```
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4980849Z 
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4981117Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4981529Z 
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4982899Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4984462Z 
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4984639Z ```bash
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4985091Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4985935Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4986750Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4987075Z 
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4987549Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4988798Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4989609Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4990077Z ```
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4990289Z 
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4991022Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4991906Z 
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4992076Z ```bash
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4992823Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4993696Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4994392Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4994835Z 
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4995229Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4996002Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4996542Z ```
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4996751Z 
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4996961Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4997759Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4998896Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-09-01T03:28:06.4999843Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-09-01T03:28:06.5000814Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-09-01T03:28:06.5001876Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-09-01T03:28:06.5002400Z 
2026-09-01T03:28:06.5002579Z ### Notes
2026-09-01T03:28:06.5002790Z 
2026-09-01T03:28:06.5003399Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-09-01T03:28:06.5004777Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-09-01T03:28:06.5005999Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-09-01T03:28:06.5007219Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-09-01T03:28:06.5008573Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-09-01T03:28:06.5009687Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-09-01T03:28:06.5010652Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-09-01T03:28:06.5011331Z </mcp-clis>
2026-09-01T03:28:06.5011735Z <github-context>
2026-09-01T03:28:06.5012333Z The following GitHub context information is available for this workflow:

2026-09-01T03:28:06.5025812Z relevant top Hacker News stories on technology that can be used today
2026-09-01T03:28:06.5026648Z by large companies. Every weekday, fetch the top 30 stories from the

2026-09-01T03:28:06.5029307Z engineering, cloud infrastructure, AI/ML, developer tooling, or

2026-09-01T03:28:06.5031768Z why it is relevant to enterprise developers. Create a GitHub issue
